info.title: SpeakUp
info.description:
AI-assisted assessment of English speaking against CEFR A1-C2.

A study aid, not a certification service: the system produces an **estimate**, and a teacher makes the final decision. Every report carries the versions of the model, features and thresholds that produced it.

Interface text is Vietnamese by requirement (SRS); this API documentation and all identifiers are English.

actually exist.

replaced with a code sent to the email (D079). Only students sign
themselves up; a teacher or an administrator is given their role by
somebody with authority (FR-32).

patch.description:
Set the sign-in email and the full name (D071).

Adding a first email needs nothing more: the person is signed in. Changing
one the account already signs in with needs the password, as changing the
password does -- otherwise a borrowed session could move the account to
another address and lock its owner out. A wrong password counts as a failed
login (NFR-07), and while the account is locked even the right one is
refused with 429 (SEC-03): the shared `reauthenticate` keeps one counter.

get.description:
Where the gateway sends the browser back. Applies the result the address stands for.

Works without a session on purpose: a session that expired while the
person was paying must not lose the payment. The page shows only what the
gateway vouched for, and the plan it bought. `left=1` is this system's own
mark on the address of a payer who left the gateway's page without paying
(payOS's cancel address): nothing is settled, the payment simply expires.

get.description:
Export the learner's own verified results. FR-38.

Only teacher-verified rows. If none exist the array is empty and the note
says so: never guess a band to fill the file.

The learner's own results in time order, with the trend named plainly. FR-27.

The trend is the difference between the first and last third of the series,
and it is reported only from five results onward: two attempts a week apart
differ by measurement noise as much as by learning (`ridge_resp_v2` has an
RMSE of 0.53 on its own validation data).

post.description:
Delete my account and everything of mine, for good (D101, FR-103).

Students only: a teacher's lessons and reviews are other people's work too,
so an administrator removes those accounts. The person types their email
again. The data goes first, then the account, so a failure
half way leaves an account that can try again. Payments and the run ledger
stay, as accounts must; they keep only the random account id.

schema.title: Response Delete My Account Api V1 Me Delete Account Post

post.description:
An administrator deletes an account of any role, for good.

The same path as a learner's own deletion (D101): the person's recordings,
reports and lesson attempts go first, then the account and its sessions.
The administrator types the account's email again, or its id when it has
no email (FR-104). Payments and the run
ledger stay with the random account id. What a teacher made for others
(lessons, review decisions) stays; the account leaves every class.

Not one's own account: whoever asks is an administrator, so the last
administrator can never be deleted.

get.description:
The submission screen; the product page for a visitor (D026).

A teacher or an administrator, who has nothing to submit, goes to the start
page of the role. The thresholds quoted are the ones in force.

The login form, with Google next to it when this instance has it turned on (D029).

`?google=<code>` says why a Google round trip came back here; only known
codes are shown, as fixed sentences.
A student opens an account with a password (D065).
A forgotten password: a code by email (D079); with email off, whom to ask.

What A1 to C2 describe, and what the machine measures of each aspect (D028, D059).

Open to visitors too: it explains a result, it does not show one. The five
thresholds are those of the model in force, the same numbers `to_band` uses.
What a run pack is and how it is paid; no refunds (D099, D102). Open to all.

The signed-in person's own account: profile, security, history, data (D028, D029).

`?google=<code>` reports how a Google round trip ended. Only known codes are
shown, as fixed sentences: nothing typed into the URL reaches the page.
A student's own submission history. FR-04.
Processing progress screen. FR-05.

AccountCreate.title: AccountCreate
AccountCreate.description: The emails of the accounts to make, all of one role.

AuditEntry.title: AuditEntry
AuditEntry.description:
Mot dong nhat ky kiem toan. FR-31.

Giu AI DA LAM GI, khong giu NOI DUNG da lam. Mot dong audit mang theo ban
sao cua bai nop hoac cua diem se bien chinh no thanh mot ban luu thu hai,
va luc do lenh xoa du lieu ca nhan khong con xoa het.

Band.title: Band
Band.description: The six CEFR levels, lowest first (D059). The order is meaningful.

ContactChange.title: ContactChange
ContactChange.description: D071: the sign-in email and the full name; either may be left out.

Criterion.title: Criterion
Criterion.description: The five in-scope CEFR criteria. Interaction was dropped per QD-04.

EraseRequest.title: EraseRequest
EraseRequest.description:
Erasure request. The email is sent twice on purpose.

This deletes audio from disk and cannot be undone, so the second field is
the only thing between a mistyped email and somebody else's data. FR-35.

Lesson.title: Lesson
Lesson.description: One lesson: a model text, its key words and a ladder of steps.

LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest
LoginRequest.description: Login payload. The password is never written to the log.

Mission.title: Mission
Mission.description:
One mission of a practice task, written in the task bank. D023.

`label` is the sentence the student reads BEFORE speaking, so the rule and
the promise must be one: "use at least 3 linking words" means `target` is 3
and `words` lists the linking words that count. `words` is used only by
USE_WORDS; READ_ALOUD compares against the task's own reference passage.

MissionKind.title: MissionKind
MissionKind.description:
Seven kinds of practice mission, each one a fixed rule applied to the recording. D023.

Each kind measures something the learner can check by listening to their own
recording: how long they spoke, where the longest pause was, which words they
used. None of them is a criterion score -- the model only learns the overall
label (see `CriterionIndicator`).

ProfileChange.title: ProfileChange
ProfileChange.description: Any subset of the profile; each value must come from its list.

Review.title: Review
Review.description:
Mot lan giang vien giu hoac sua ket qua. FR-30, FR-31.

Truoc day `Repository.review_history` tra ve `list[dict]`, nghia la hinh
dang cua mot quyet dinh duyet chi ton tai trong dau nguoi viet cau SQL.
Day la thu ma ca he thong ton tai de phuc vu -- no xung dang co mot lop.

Luu y `old_*` co the rong: mot bai ma may tu choi cham van duoc duyet, va
khi do khong co gi de "sua tu".

ReviewClose.title: ReviewClose
ReviewClose.description: Dong mot bai may khong cham duoc. Ly do bat buoc, nhu moi quyet dinh duyet.

ReviewDecision.title: ReviewDecision
ReviewDecision.description:
A teacher's decision. The reason is mandatory so the change stays traceable.

There is deliberately NO reviewer_id field. The reviewer's identity comes
from the login session, not from data the caller declares about itself.
Before iteration 2 the client sent this field, so the audit log only
recorded an arbitrary string and could not prove who changed a score.

Role.title: Role
Role.description: The three roles defined by FR-32.

SignupRequest.title: SignupRequest
SignupRequest.description:
Self sign-up (D065, D071): the email to sign in with, the full name a
teacher reads, a password.

Step.title: Step
Step.description: One exercise of a lesson, as the teacher configured it.

Topic.title: Topic
Topic.description:
What a unit talks about (D027). The path runs A1 → C2 (D059), and within each
level the units change topic, so practice stays varied as the level rises.
